A1.justification: Both PDFs describe CFG-Bench with the same four-tier framework and core experiments. Their complete main texts, tables, figures, prompts, and appendices support comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original model evaluations, fine-tuning transfer experiments, FPS ablations, and human-baseline and annotator-agreement results.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and adds Gemini-3-Pro results, a FAVOR-data fine-tuning comparison, and human–LLM and cross-evaluator reliability results.

M1.justification: The benchmark's reported counterfactual gating procedure changes: v1 requires explicit rejection of a false premise, whereas v3 Section 3.3 and Table S7 also accept implicit factual correction. The four-tier framework and QA-generation pipeline remain intact. Newly disclosed LoRA settings do not establish a changed training method.

E1.justification: Table 4 newly uses FAVOR's motion-level data as an alternative fine-tuning corpus. The five-source CFG video corpus, eleven evaluation tasks, and downstream EB-ALFRED and EB-Manipulation coverage remain unchanged.

E2.justification: v3 adds Gemini-3-Pro to Table 2 and Qwen2.5-VL-7B fine-tuned on FAVOR data to Table 4. Existing comparator models remain; removing the Qwen2.5-VL-7B 16-FPS row removes a configuration, not that comparator.

E3.justification: Reported closed/open QA counts change from 9,282/10,280 to 9,165/10,397, and counterfactual scoring now permits implicit correction. v3 adds a 4,200-response, six-expert validation protocol and an alternative-evaluator comparison, while removing Qwen2.5-VL-7B's 16-FPS condition. These reported changes do not establish that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: New Section 4.4 substantially extends validation through human–LLM agreement and sensitivity to replacing DeepSeek-R1 with Claude-Sonnet-4. The FAVOR fine-tuning comparison additionally tests whether transfer benefits are specific to CFG data. Annotator agreement, most FPS ablations, QA-format comparisons, and error cases already existed in v1.

E5.justification: v3 adds human–LLM agreement estimates and Spearman correlation between evaluator-induced rankings. Its stated threshold for high agreement changes from 0.80 to 0.67. Three-evaluation averages and human-baseline 95% confidence intervals were already reported in v1 and remain; no increased repeat count is established.

E6.justification: Most shared results are numerically unchanged. Gemini-3-Pro newly leads Table 2 with 65.60% closed-ended accuracy and 5.67 open-ended score; Qwen2.5-VL-7B's 16-FPS results disappear. Table 4 adds FAVOR-trained averages of 4.3/8.2, retaining CFG-trained 9.7/15.3. New reliability results include human–LLM alpha of 0.74/0.75 and evaluator-ranking correlation of 0.92.

T1.justification: Neither version develops formal theorems, proofs, or mathematical derivations that change between versions. Replacing the cognitive framework's inspiration with Norman's Action Cycle is conceptual positioning, not a new formal theory.

C1.justification: Both versions claim a four-tier benchmark for fine-grained embodied action intelligence, expose current MLLMs' deficiencies, and claim that CFG-data fine-tuning improves embodied planning and manipulation. Revised contribution wording and additional supporting experiments preserve these central claims.

C2.justification: v3 adds substantive interpretations concerning evaluator reliability, evaluation bias, tier-specific transfer mechanisms, and training recommendations. It attributes the FAVOR comparison to limitations of motion-level supervision, qualifies the FPS bottleneck explanation, and removes v1 Appendix B2's Moravec's Paradox interpretation. The explicit limitations in Appendix E remain unchanged.

D1.justification: New Appendix B3 supplies previously absent SFT details: LoRA, 800 epochs, AdamW, learning rate 1e-6, batch size 8, eight H200 GPUs, cross-entropy loss, a 90.3%/9.7% train/validation split, and tier-balanced sampling. Figure S4 adds annotation and video-discarding guidelines. v3 also adds a project-page link. These materially expand reproducibility documentation.

R1.justification: The framework's grounding changes from Card's GOMS framework, called GMOS in v1, to Norman's Action Cycle with explicit tier mappings. Moravec's citation and discussion disappear; MotionSight, BEAR, and additional model references are added. The central positioning against descriptive action benchmarks and complementary embodied benchmarks remains.

P1.justification: v3 makes targeted paragraph and terminology edits, simplifies dataset-generation subheadings, and reorganizes supporting material around a new Reliability Analysis section. Annotator agreement moves from the appendix into that section. Most existing task descriptions, related-work prose, and conclusions remain closely matched.

P2.justification: The document changes from two-column to single-column layout with extensively resized displays. v1 Figures 3–4 merge into v3 Figure 3, Figures 6–7 merge into Figure 4, and Figure 5 moves to Appendix Figure S1. v3 adds an annotation-guideline figure, inserts human scores into existing example figures, and restructures appendix tables and prompt displays.

improvement.justification: The added human–LLM and evaluator-sensitivity checks address validation missing from v1, while the FAVOR comparison and SFT/annotation details strengthen evidence and reproducibility. These benefits are limited by an inconsistent revised rubric: Table S7 accepts implicit correction, but Table S8 retains an explicit-rejection requirement. Shared scores also remain unchanged despite revised QA counts and scoring instructions, without explaining whether rescoring occurred.
